title: Practice 4: Genitive endings: nouns, adjectives, pronouns

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Старайтесь не допускать ___ (стилистический) ошибок в речи.
exercises.prompt: Take care to avoid stylistic errors while speaking.
exercises.why: However, there is a peculiarity in Russian when counting: though we use the genitive singular on nouns that are numbered 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, etc, we use the genitive *plural* for any adjectives attached to that noun: *Три кни́жных магази́на Пять книжных магази́нов Он зна́ет сто два ру́сских сло́ва Он зна́ет сто шесть ру́сских слов* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
exercises.context: However, there is a peculiarity in Russian when counting: though we use the genitive singular on nouns that are numbered 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, etc, we use the genitive *plural* for any adjectives attached to that noun:

exercises.prompt: I think we should stick to the original plan.
exercises.why: Like nouns, masculine and neuter adjectives have the same ending in the genitive singular, **-ого**, pronounced 'oh-vo'. — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
exercises.context: Like nouns, masculine and neuter adjectives have the same ending in the genitive singular, **-ого**, pronounced 'oh-vo'.
